record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports weight edits using difference-of-means refusal directions and measures refusal outcomes, but this is not the original activation-ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports practical weight-edit results and grounding-retention comparisons. It also reports geometry and an MoE write attribution; these are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the listed versions. The Qwen3.6-35B-A3B result gives a post-edit refusal count without a stated pre-edit count.
record.test_reason: The repo applies difference-in-means refusal-direction weight edits (standard and oblique abliteration) to released Qwen models and reports refusal outcomes. This bears directly on V2. It is a tool repo, and the evidence is weak: substring refusal counting, a single seed, and small n.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say standard abliteration removes refusal but also damages hedging, so models fabricate instead of saying they don't know. Their oblique projector fixes that side effect at matched refusal removal. They ship edits on two larger Qwen models and stress that the results are Qwen-only, single-seed, use substring refusal counting and first-token KL, and are not a general claim.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo, not a replication. It uses difference-of-means refusal directions but searches a depth-shaped, per-layer edit and applies an oblique projector as a weight edit; the README says the original direction and basic abliteration are established practice.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says full-depth search can place the kernel at layer 0 and yield KL between 1.0 and 2.5, whereas its bounded search reaches KL well under 0.1. Results are reported for one seed per model and regime.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched refusal removal on Qwen3-4B, the oblique projector retains 96% of hedging versus 71% for standard abliteration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An oblique projector preserves a named second behaviour better than standard abliteration at equal refusal removal.

fits_no_version.finding: Median absolute cosine between the refusal and hedging directions in the upper layers is 0.04–0.17 across three Qwen models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal and hedging directions are nearly orthogonal in Qwen models.

fits_no_version.finding: First-token KL on harmless prompts after the edit is 0.276 (MoE) and 0.060 (27B dense).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First-token KL damage after abliteration varies by architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Qwen3.6 MoE, the refusal write splits 4.6% attention, 43.5% shared expert and 52% routed experts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fused MoEs, most of the refusal write passes through the expert stacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Unmatched harmful/harmless prompt sets rotated the extracted direction roughly 35 degrees away from the matched direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means refusal direction extraction is sensitive to prompt-set matching.

record.problems: The README reports one seed per model and regime and says its refusal count is substring matching. KL is first-token only on harmless prompts and does not address long-form degradation. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has no stated pre-edit refusal count; there are no non-Qwen model results.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows left out.

untested.parts: Non-Qwen families (the README says Llama, Mistral, Gemma and DeepSeek were not tested); long-form capability retention; robust refusal judging beyond substring matching.
Activation ablation at all layers and positions, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and broad capability evaluation.
All. Rank>1 preservation is untested, and the second direction concerns hedging, not refusal.

missing.what: Full-depth search placed the kernel at layer 0, giving KL 1.0–2.5 (destroyed model), versus KL under 0.1 with bounded search.
missing.locator: README, How it works, The pipeline

missing.what: Unmatched prompt pairs caused a roughly 35-degree rotation of the refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool repo rather than a replication. The refusal counts have no stated n beyond 40 prompts, and there is no pre-edit baseline for the MoE (r5 stays cannot_determine). Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 model names and the 2026 dates are as given in the README.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not test removal of one fixed direction from every layer and position, adding that direction to induce harmless-request refusals, or broadly measuring general capability under that original intervention.
The README reports weight-edit refusal results on Qwen models, but does not establish generalization to other model families.
No attack suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The distinct direction discussed is for hedging, not evidence that refusal itself is affine, a cone, or carried by multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other model-variant transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or timing is reported.
